headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress paired with social-auto-upload’s account/API posting creates default data-exfiltration and compliance risk; prompt-injection and conflict risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, Airbyte can move data via APIs and social-auto-upload consumes files and posts content, so a manual copy/paste or file handoff could bridge them. The pathway is plausible but not default, and the blast radius is limited to the transferred content.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airbyte output into files consumed by social-auto-upload
IF a shared workspace or clipboard is used between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Disable copy/paste handoff between outputs and upload inputs
Review any transferred text before upload
Use a staging file with manual approval
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and touches business data, while social-auto-upload handles account data and also has broad egress. Even without a shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive business or account data to external services by default through their respective APIs, creating an exfiltration and retention risk.
conditions: IF Airbyte connectors ingest business data that is later passed to social-auto-upload
IF social-auto-upload posts content derived from Airbyte outputs to third-party platforms
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive test data
Block outbound traffic except to approved endpoints
Redact account identifiers before transfer
Audit uploaded payloads before posting
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte exposes API-based data integration, while social-auto-upload has no filesystem write, git, or shell privileges. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource or locking issue, so write-write conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because Airbyte’s broader write surfaces are not fully enumerated, so the lower severity is chosen cautiously.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external account or API resource
IF Airbyte writes records that social-auto-upload also edits in the same session
mitigations: Assign separate accounts or namespaces
Serialize access to shared external resources
Use read-only mode for one agent
Check for duplicate writes before execution
requires-engineering: add resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can generate transformed business data that social-auto-upload may then publish through platform APIs. That creates a plausible chain where B treats A’s output as ready-to-post content without verification. The pair does not show explicit downstream automation beyond posting, so this is not high, but the default handoff can still propagate errors.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is used as the source for social-auto-upload posts
IF social-auto-upload publishes content without human review
mitigations: Insert a manual review step before posting
Validate schema and content before upload
Use a dry-run account first
Compare outputs against source records
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, while social-auto-upload handles account data and posts to external social platforms. That combination can create residency, retention, and disclosure mismatches by default if regulated or sensitive business data is routed into public posting workflows. The profiles do not show a DPA or residency control, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF regulated business data is ingested by Airbyte
IF any of that data is forwarded into social-auto-upload for publication
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use synthetic or anonymized datasets
Document retention and deletion rules
Restrict posting to pre-approved content
requires-engineering: add residency and DPA controls
